researched_from: Robert's Rules of Order (Newly Revised, 12th ed.)
BoardSource: The Source - Twelve Principles of Governance
clarified_task_template: Produce executive meeting minutes from the attached transcript following industry best practice. Past tense, neutral voice, paraphrased (not verbatim). Output must include in order: (1) header block w/ title, date, start-end, duration, type, quorum status; (2) attendees split into present (in-person vs remote), absent/excused, guests, chair, minute-taker; (3) ONE-paragraph executive TLDR stating what was achieved + most material outcome (1-3 sentences max); (4) TOP-3 RANKED key actions - the 3 highest-impact items, each w/ action verb, named owner, explicit due date, priority; (5) decisions taken (separate from actions - decisions are immutable record of what was settled, format 'Body approved X', include vote count if applicable, effective date); (6) full action-items table w/ columns Action | Owner | Due | Status | Notes; (7) discussion summary by agenda item (2-3 neutral sentences each); (8) risks / parking-lot raised but deferred; (9) next meeting date + agenda preview; (10) source attribution line. Confidentiality classification at top if material. Every owner + due date must come from the transcript verbatim or be marked '[TBD - verify with attendees]'. Never invent attendees, statements, decisions, owners, or dates.

action_items_full.owner_rule: named person from transcript or [TBD - verify with attendees]

voice_rules: decisions in active voice (Board approved X)
actions in imperative voice w/ explicit owner
quote only material statements w/ attribution
must_haves: every action has a named owner OR [TBD - verify with attendees]
every action has an explicit due date OR [TBD], never ASAP/soon
top-3 ranked actions distinct from full action-items table
confidentiality classification at top if material
must_avoid: magazine-style layout - hero blocks, dek, pull-quotes, sparklines
fabricated names, statements, decisions, action items, owners, dates
padding to hit a word count
red_team_checklist: Is every attendee actually in the transcript?
Is every action item supported by a verbatim transcript quote?
Is every owner + due date either explicit in transcript or marked [TBD]?
Is the top-3 ranking defensible (highest-impact, not most-recent)?
Would this minutes pass a board chair's read in 2 minutes?
Is past tense + neutral voice maintained throughout?
Does the parking lot capture every deferred item?

output_format_recommendations.default: minimal HTML w/ tables, NOT magazine-grade editorial
output_format_recommendations.html_structure: header > attendees > tldr > top-3 (h2) > decisions (h2) > action items (table) > discussion (h2) > parking (h2) > next meeting (footer)
output_format_recommendations.no_decoration: no hero, no dek, no pull-quotes, no sparklines, no font-features beyond tabular-nums
output_format_recommendations.print_friendly: @media print stylesheet, page-break-inside avoid on tables
